briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and Anthropic Claude 4 race intensifies multi-agent capabilities

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AI frontier continues rapid expansion with new model releases and massive compute investments. Competition between US and Chinese labs drives both capability gains and regulatory scrutiny. Prompt injection threats persist across deployed systems.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI released o4 with advanced multi-agent orchestration while Anthropic launched Claude 4 Opus. Google DeepMind unveiled Gemini 3 and Meta open-sourced Llama 4. xAI scaled Colossus to 200k H100s for Grok-3 training.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New NIST guidelines target agentic AI risks amid rising exploits.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: Microsoft and Google announced new 50k GPU clusters in Texas and Nevada. TSMC reports 3nm yield improvements for next-gen AI chips. Energy constraints slow European data center builds.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will multi-agent systems achieve autonomous goal alignment before 2028?
